 November 18, 2026 
 News , Richmond 
 Same day voter registration increases over half since last midterm election
 Illustration by Jackson Bechtold. 
 Skye Hathaway , Copy Editor 
 Richmond saw a significant increase in same day voter registration on Nov. 3, with numbers up 52.14% from the 2022 midterm election, according to unofficial results from the Virginia Department of Elections .  
 Richmonders cast 3,303 SDR provisional ballots on Election Day, marking a record high since the 2024 presidential election, according to VDOE.   
 Citizens may cast a provisional ballot when registering to vote early or same day. Richmonders may choose SDR if they missed the initial registration deadline or reside in a different locality than the one they are registered in.  
 Gray Ryan, a second-year communication arts student, cast his provisional ballot because he changed his registration location the day before the deadline. He said he worried that his application would not make it to the registrar’s office in time to vote.  
 “I originally registered in Charlottesville, my hometown,” Ryan said. “Usually I go back there but my ride back there this year fell through, so I had to make some changes last minute.” 
 Ryan said several concerns drove him to the polls, including lowering gas prices and approving the 1% sales tax to increase funding for Richmond Public Schools.  
 “There were a number of issues I cared about on the ballot, namely among them marriage rights for intersex and interracial couples,” Ryan said. “I’m in an interracial relationship so, obviously, that has some personal importance to me.” 
 This November’s young voter turnout was the second highest of any midterm election in the last 30 years, according to the Center for Information and Research on Civic Learning and Engagement .  
 “I think a lot of this election was influenced by the younger vote and people coming together to say collectively, ‘Hey, our future’s not really looking too bright right now and we want people in power who will ensure that it becomes bright,” Ryan said.  
 Patrick Lydell lives and works in Richmond, but moved from Northern Virginia in the summer. After realizing that he missed the deadline to change his address, he decided to reregister on Election Day to cast his vote.  
 Lydell said he feels that citizens’ ability to influence what happens in their government is one of the few positives about U.S. democracy.  
 “I think it’s an important civic responsibility of people that live in the United States to go out and vote in every single election,” Lydell said. “It’s just important for me as a person, because I have the right to do that. It’s something I’m proud to be able to do.”
